contents.name: §§6.4.1 and 6.5: QED interaction, tree-current cancellation, and coefficient rules

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete §6.4.1 current-conservation argument through the explicit on-shell Dirac equations, then the full §6.5 vertex, photon-line, fermion-line and external-line table.
source_review.supports: The adopted formal rule symbols: electron vertex -ie gamma, Feynman-gauge photon line, and Dirac free-line numerator and mass-shell denominator.
source_review.limitations: Tong uses signature (+---), D=partial+ieA for the electron, and its own gamma convention. The item maps these to the local h=-eta and charge conventions explicitly. The source gives a formal diagram rule table, not a convergent or nonperturbative QED construction.

source_review.read_extent: Read equations 6.578–6.584, including the on-shell spinor equations and the contraction of the longitudinal momentum with each external current.
source_review.supports: The familiar tree-level current-conservation context for a gauge-longitudinal photon term.
source_review.limitations: The item proves only its finite/formal/tree scope from its exact planned matrix and current suppliers; Tong’s broader all-diagram sentence is not imported, and no loop theorem is claimed.

contents.name: §6.7: omitted loop corrections
contents.reason: The assigned theorem is coefficientwise finite/formal and tree-level only; it does not claim loop products, renormalization, all-orders Ward identities, or continuum scattering.

sources.title: John B. Kogut, An Introduction to Lattice Gauge Theory and Spin Systems, Reviews of Modern Physics 51 (1979)
sources.locator: Complete 55-page review; relevant Hamiltonian and Gauss-law treatment in §VI.C, printed pp. 694–696. The Rome1 PDF is byte-identical to the previously retrieved full text.

contents.name: §VI.C: compact angle, quantized link electric variable, Hamiltonian, and local gauge generator

source_review.read_extent: Read §VI.C from the anisotropic-action Hamiltonian construction and angular-link/electric commutator through the integer electric spectrum, Hamiltonian, local gauge transformations, Gauss generator, and charged flux-line dressing.
source_review.supports: The physical model context for compact U(1) link rotors, integer electric labels, Hamiltonian terms, Gauss constraints and boundary-flux dressing.
source_review.limitations: Kogut treats a cubic spatial lattice and its source-specific scaling conventions. The authored item uses the separately defined abstract finite graph, assigns units explicitly, proves operator domains locally, and asserts no continuum limit.

contents.name: §VI.C: local gauge invariance and physical Gauss constraint

source_review.read_extent: Read the local gauge-generator and physical-state discussion in the same full §VI.C section.
source_review.supports: The role of the gauge-invariant physical sector and its Gauss constraint in the adopted regulator.
source_review.limitations: Kogut does not prove the exact maximal domains, nonempty projection, or self-adjoint physical dynamics claimed here; those are conditional deductions from the inspected local mathematical suppliers.

source_review.read_extent: Read the charge-source and contour operator discussion through its computation that the link factors change electric flux along the path.
source_review.supports: The physical motivation for requiring charged insertions to be accompanied by boundary electric flux.
source_review.limitations: The thought experiment proves only the stated exact finite-graph commutation obstruction from Gauss law. It does not assert a continuum charged-sector theorem or import Kogut’s strong-coupling approximation.

contents.name: §§2.1–2.2: compact U(1) rotor links, integer electric labels, fermionic matter, and physical Gauss sector

source_review.read_extent: Read §§2.1–2.2 from the compact angle and U(1) group-element link Hilbert space through the integer electric basis, minimally coupled fermion hopping, Gauss generators, and the physical charge-zero sector.

source_review.limitations: Their worked model is a two-dimensional staggered-fermion construction. The authored item instead adopts the finite graph/CAR data of its exact local definition and does not claim a continuum Dirac limit.
